minutes.headline: Selectmen debated a new HR assistant town manager post and set a one-vote rule for the land acquisition committee.
minutes.summary: Public and board comment centered on the proposed assistant town manager/HR position and a part-time parks director in the town manager's budget. The board amended an alcohol license, endorsed a cycling fundraiser, updated senior tax work-off rules, and made committee appointments. It split on land acquisition committee makeup and on how 2-2 votes are worded in the town meeting warrant.

what_happened.line: The board voted that each land acquisition committee seat is held by one person with one vote.
A motion to add two members at large to the land acquisition committee failed.
The chair will ask conservation to name one member for the committee, to be confirmed at the next meeting.
The board amended the senior tax work-off rules, raising the hourly rate to the state minimum and raising the abatement cap.
Board and public comment questioned a new HR director/assistant town manager post; on 2-2 warrant articles, the board will state no recommendation.

why_it_matters: A new town manager position would be paid from the town budget, mostly taxes, and the debate is whether that money fits ahead of schools or public safety.
The land acquisition committee shapes which open space purchases reach Town Meeting, and the one-seat, one-vote rule sets who decides.
Residents who work off taxes should see a higher hourly rate and abatement cap.
